task.title: Harden the owned-definition guard test in hosted.rs
task.description:
Filed from the P6-039 adversarial review (2026-08-09). The structural guard test (owned_definition_guard in app/src/backend/hosted.rs) asserts the inline owned-per-oracle aggregation never reappears, but the substring needle is (a) bypassable — a re-derived aggregate with different aliases, reversed join order, a comma-join, or GROUP BY 1 sails past it — and (b) able to false-fail — the needle has no terminator, so a legitimate future per-board breakdown (GROUP BY p.oracle_id, h.board) would trip it. Harden the matcher to catch re-derivations by structure rather than exact spelling (e.g. token-normalize the SQL before matching) without tripping on collection- or board-scoped aggregations, which are legitimate different computations.

Extended after the P6-110 adversarial review (2026-08-09) — the soft_delete_guard module has the same class of gaps: (a) the ownership-lookup guard pins only the literal 'SELECT 1 FROM collections WHERE id = $1' idiom, so a rewritten check (SELECT id ..., different spacing, different bind index) passes silently; (b) no guard covers collection_view's metadata read (hosted.rs:846), the other dominating gate that makes the per-collection aggregate exemptions sound; (c) the migration-text test greps 0010 only, so a later migration re-replacing owned_by_card without the deleted_at filter or without security_invoker goes undetected.

Optional tidy while there: collection_tree's d.desired_total is an uncast sum(quantity) while shopping_list casts ::int — harmless asymmetry the review noted. Specs: specs/collection-api.md, specs/collection-deletion.md.
